chain.title: Share of 311 closures that record a hand-off, not finished work
chain.plain: We took every 311 request the city closed in 2025-26 (city open data, csb.zip), counted each request once, and read the words the city closed it with. About 35 in every 100 closures say the job was scheduled, referred, added to a rotation or turned into a work order, not that it was done; the table of closing words and how each was classed can be downloaded and overruled.
chain.label: observed

chain.title: Requests that came back, and repairs that did not hold
chain.plain: Of requests the city closed in 2025-26, about 7 in 100 were reported again at the same address for the same problem within a month. For weekly services like refuse that often means the problem came back; for repairs that should last, about 3 in 100 were reported again within two weeks.
chain.label: observed

sources.name: 311 service requests (Citizens' Service Bureau), yearly CSVs in csb.zip

joins: Same normalised PROBADDRESS and PROBLEMCODE, filed strictly after DATETIMECLOSED.
corrections: Counted once per REQUESTID: the city's CSV repeats a request once per caller (349,031 rows hold 322,104 requests in 2024-26).
Called 'came back', not false closure: refuse is weekly and dumping recurs at chronic sites.
Report B's 23.7% 'repeat' counted any two requests in 12 months; replaced by this post-closure measure.
bounds: 'Public Nuisance Rpt' closes automatically on submission, so its rate is structural.
The normaliser merges spellings, so N1's rates run slightly above raw-text matching.
Not reproduced exactly: N8's independent recompute gets 6.1% (10,790) against the registry's 7.0% (11,978), cause unexplained; quote 'about 6 to 7 in 100'.

chain.title: Cave-ins: referral versus repair
chain.plain: In the southwest, cave-in requests are mostly closed within a day as 'referred to street maintenance for repair work to be scheduled'; in the north the same referral takes about six weeks. Where the words say 'work completed' the wait is about 8 days against 23, but too few southwest repairs are recorded that way to call it proven.
chain.label: observed

sources.name: 311 service requests (Citizens' Service Bureau), yearly CSVs in csb.zip
Closure-class rule table (the city's exact closing text mapped to done / hand-off / converted / no action / other / blank)

corrections: Counted once per REQUESTID: the city's CSV repeats a request once per caller (349,031 rows hold 322,104 requests in 2024-26).
Resident channels only (web, phone, email, chat, Twitter, letter); a request counts as resident-filed if any caller was a resident.
This replaces the earlier '1.7 vs 27.6 days' headline, which compared quick referrals in the southwest with completed work in the north.
bounds: Referral time jumps from at most 1.1 days in every ward 1-5 to at least 15.7 in every ward 6-14: a process line, not repair speed (inferred). No public file holds repair dates for referred cave-ins.
Only 35 'work completed' closures in wards 1-5, so the repair-speed gap is unproven.
Use 41.7 (N8 settled): it comes from the published WARD column, which an analyst can reproduce without GIS. The Monday brief's 41.1 (367/116) fills 2,425 blank wards from the ward map; footnote it.

chain.title: Single light out, 'work completed', by ward group (failed robustness)
chain.plain: For one streetlight out, closed with the words 'work completed', residents in the north waited about 41 days and in the southwest about 16, against the city's promise of 3, but only for requests filed between October 2025 and March 2026; before the tornado the waits were nearly equal. We show it as an episode, not as a standing gap.

bounds: Whole-block outages show no gap (0.7 vs 0.7 days).

chain.label: observed

sources.name: Forestry property maintenance service records (the forestry billing ledger)
Land Reutilization Authority inventory (city-owned land-bank parcels)

joins: Ledger PARCEL to LRA ParcelId (the synthesis's first attempt used a column the LRA file lacks and wrongly returned zero; corrected).
corrections: LRA join corrected (see joins).

The ledger repeats rows (N8): 2019 has 112,734 cut rows but 55,624 distinct parcel-date-type entries; 2026 has 46,346 cut rows but 39,862 distinct. Parcel counts are unaffected; row counts are not cuts.
bounds: Contrast with the reported quote: CityStat's manager said in August that per-lot mowing 'we don't have that tracked in a system' (First Alert 4, 14 Aug 2026). Both can be true: a billing charge is not an operations log.
2025 holds 13,168 cut rows on 8,780 parcels against 46,346 on 16,118 in 2026; why is not established.

chain.title: The city's own per-lot cut record
chain.plain: The city's forestry billing ledger, published on its open-data portal, records a dated charge for every grass cut it bills to a parcel. In 2026 it bills cuts on about 12,000 lots, 7,425 of them owned by the city's land bank: the per-lot record the city has said it does not have.
chain.label: observed

sources.name: Forestry property maintenance service records (the forestry billing ledger)
Land Reutilization Authority inventory (city-owned land-bank parcels)

joins: Ledger PARCEL to LRA ParcelId (the synthesis's first attempt used a column the LRA file lacks and wrongly returned zero; corrected).
corrections: LRA join corrected (see joins).

The ledger repeats rows (N8): 2019 has 112,734 cut rows but 55,624 distinct parcel-date-type entries; 2026 has 46,346 cut rows but 39,862 distinct. Parcel counts are unaffected; row counts are not cuts.
bounds: Contrast with the reported quote: CityStat's manager said in August that per-lot mowing 'we don't have that tracked in a system' (First Alert 4, 14 Aug 2026). Both can be true: a billing charge is not an operations log.
2025 holds 13,168 cut rows on 8,780 parcels against 46,346 on 16,118 in 2026; why is not established.

n1_mowing_gaps.definition: Parcels on the 2026 mowing rotation (at least one Grass Maint cut 1 Apr-30 Sep); median longest gap between consecutive billed cuts; parcels that went more than 42 and more than 90 days without a billed cut (counting the run from the last cut to 30 Sep, so lots cut once count too); parcels cut once; LRA parcels over 90 days; and parcels with more than 90 days strictly between two cuts.
n1_mowing_gaps.label: observed
n1_mowing_gaps.note: Say 'went more than 90 days without a billed cut (counting to 30 September)' (N8 finding 15d). The city's rotation runs about eight weeks between cuts, so BUILD-SPEC's 42-day threshold flags almost every lot.
n1_mowing_gaps.derivation: the Forestry Division's service ledger (forestry-service-records.csv, cuts = 'Grass Maint' and 'Weed-Grass' rows), parcel ids looked up in the LRA inventory; a cut is a distinct parcel and date. Posting dates are batched weekly, so gaps are good to about a week.

chain.title: Mowing look-back: gaps between cuts on rotation lots
chain.plain: Looking back at the 2026 season in the city's own ledger, the typical rotation lot's longest wait between billed cuts was about eight weeks; about 3,900 lots, 2,200 of them land-bank lots, went more than 90 days without a billed cut (counting to 30 September).
chain.label: observed

sources.name: Forestry property maintenance service records (the forestry billing ledger)
Land Reutilization Authority inventory (city-owned land-bank parcels)

corrections: The ledger is a billing record, not an operations log: SERVICEDATE is a posting date batched by about a week (8,507 of 2026's rows carry a Sunday date; 2,608 carry 23 April), so day counts are precise to the week, and a cut that was never billed looks like no cut. Say 'no cut billed', never 'never cut'.
Threshold moved from the spec's 42 days to 90 (about one and a half of the city's own cycles), because 42 days flags 96% of lots.
bounds: Lots never cut in 2026 are not on this list by construction (no first cut).

chain.title: Promises kept: closed, and closed as done, by the city's own due date
chain.plain: Every 311 request carries a date the city itself promises the work by. Of requests whose date has passed, a little over half were closed by it, but only about one in five were closed by it with words saying the work was done; the rest were closed as passed on, or not closed in time.

sources.name: 311 service requests (Citizens' Service Bureau), yearly CSVs in csb.zip
Closure-class rule table (the city's exact closing text mapped to done / hand-off / converted / no action / other / blank)

corrections: Counted once per REQUESTID: the city's CSV repeats a request once per caller (349,031 rows hold 322,104 requests in 2024-26).

Closing words classed by the reviewable table in research/chapters/N2-closure-classes.csv (drafted by an AI model, applied by SQL; a second agent's independent rules agree on 98.4% of closures; no human review yet).

PRJCOMPLETEDATE is filled on 97.9% of 2024-26 requests and is a fixed offset per type (light 3 days, cave-in 3, towing 5, residential pothole 8, alley pothole 16, dumping 10, debris 3, tree inspection 14, vacant-lot weeds 14 or 90, vacant-building weeds 90).
bounds: Two denominators exist tonight: N4 drops cancelled requests (many are duplicates) and shows the cancelled share beside; N1 and N3 count them as not done. The site must say which it shows.
The city's 311 due dates differ from CityStat's published goals for 3 of 9 services (alley potholes 16 vs 17 days; whole-block lights 2 days vs 24 hours; critical signs 3 days vs 48 hours).
For weed codes the words are almost always 'on schedule', so they are graded by the ledger instead (see lot_cut_rates).

chain.title: Vacant lots closed 'on schedule': cut billed within 30 days, by season end, none in 2026
chain.plain: We matched each 2026 weed request on a vacant lot to its parcel (311 file to MSD's parcel addresses, 90% matched) and then to the city's forestry billing ledger, which records every grass cut the city charges to a parcel. Of requests the city closed as 'on schedule to be cut', about a third show a cut billed within a month and about one in five show none billed all season (21.4% of 729; a quarter if 'added to rotation' closures are counted too). The ledger posts in weekly batches, so we count weeks, not days.
chain.label: observed

sources.name: 311 service requests (Citizens' Service Bureau), yearly CSVs in csb.zip
MSD parcel attributes for St. Louis City (PID = city ParcelId, PROP_ADD), owner name dropped
sources.where: data/raw/msd/msd_parcels_stl_city_attrs.jsonl (MSD GIS, retrieved by the data audit 13 Oct 2026)

sources.name: Forestry property maintenance service records (the forestry billing ledger)

joins: 311 address normalised by one tested function (scripts/night/N1/normalise.py) and matched to MSD PROP_ADD to get the parcel id; 90.1% of 2025-26 vacant-lot and 93.3% of vacant-building weed requests matched (knock-out bar 80%).
Parcel id matched to the ledger's PARCEL; 'Grass Maint' and 'Weed-Grass' rows dated after 1995 count as cuts (the ledger uses 1900-01-01 as a placeholder).
corrections: Counted once per REQUESTID: the city's CSV repeats a request once per caller (349,031 rows hold 322,104 requests in 2024-26).

The ledger is a billing record, not an operations log: SERVICEDATE is a posting date batched by about a week (8,507 of 2026's rows carry a Sunday date; 2,608 carry 23 April), so day counts are precise to the week, and a cut that was never billed looks like no cut. Say 'no cut billed', never 'never cut'.

Mislabel corrected (N8): n1_weeds_lot_onschedule_ledger counts 'on schedule' and 'added to rotation' together (24.8% of 808 with no cut in 2026); 'on schedule to be cut' alone is 21.4% of 729 (cut within 30 days 37.2%); vacant buildings 32.2% for 'on schedule' alone.
Vacant-building lots kept apart: contractor cuts may not be billed into the ledger (only 516 'Vacant Building' Grass Maint rows in 2026), so their figures are a lower bound.
Closures reading 'no forestry violations' excluded: no cut is expected (85-86% have none).
bounds: About 10% of weed requests match no parcel (unnumbered lots, numbers outside a parcel's recorded range, spelling) and drop out.
Rests on 2026 only: the 2025 ledger is thin (8,780 parcels billed against 16,118 in 2026), consistent with crews moved to tornado debris.

n5_unsat_cut_calls_2026.label: observed
n5_unsat_cut_calls_2026.note: of 227 matched calls, 63 came within 30 days after a billed cut and 40 were on lots with no cut billed all year, so a call does not show a cut happened. N8 reports 229 / 67 / 61 with a wider join that adds address-range matches; the gap is mostly in 'no cut all year' (ours 40, N8 61).
n5_unsat_cut_calls_2026.derivation: 311 'Unsatisfy Cut - VLot' calls ('Vacant lot cut incomplete') filed in 2026, all channels, one row per request id (csb.zip), joined to a parcel by exact normalised address through MSD's parcel address file, then to distinct cut dates in the Forestry billing ledger (weekly posting batches).

chain.title: Land-bank lots closed 'on schedule' with no cut billed after
chain.plain: Among city-owned vacant lots that residents reported for weeds in 2026 and that the city closed within three days as 'on schedule to be cut', 94 requests on 75 lots show no cut billed in the city's own ledger afterwards. The lead example, on the 1700 block of N Taylor Av, was reported twice and closed within minutes both times; 36 other parcels on its city block were billed for cuts that season, and it was not.
chain.label: observed

joins: 311 address to parcel via MSD (83% of the 1,500 candidate requests matched).
Parcel to the LRA inventory (city-owned) and to the ledger.
corrections: Counted once per REQUESTID: the city's CSV repeats a request once per caller (349,031 rows hold 322,104 requests in 2024-26).

bounds: Shown at block level only, including the hero lot (Jack's ruling); ids withheld from public files.

Use N5's 94 requests on 75 lots (N8 settled; independent recompute 90 on 71, the gap is the address join). N6's brief count of 103 on 82 drops the resident filter and uses N1's wider join; it must say 'all channels' or adopt N5's rule. Requests filed after mid-September have had little time: filed by 15 Sep, 79 on 62 (N8).

chain.title: The city's own per-lot cut record
chain.plain: The city's forestry billing ledger, published on its open-data portal, records a dated charge for every grass cut it bills to a parcel. In 2026 it bills cuts on about 12,000 lots, 7,425 of them owned by the city's land bank: the per-lot record the city has said it does not have.
chain.label: observed

sources.name: Forestry property maintenance service records (the forestry billing ledger)
Land Reutilization Authority inventory (city-owned land-bank parcels)

joins: Ledger PARCEL to LRA ParcelId (the synthesis's first attempt used a column the LRA file lacks and wrongly returned zero; corrected).
corrections: LRA join corrected (see joins).

The ledger repeats rows (N8): 2019 has 112,734 cut rows but 55,624 distinct parcel-date-type entries; 2026 has 46,346 cut rows but 39,862 distinct. Parcel counts are unaffected; row counts are not cuts.
bounds: Contrast with the reported quote: CityStat's manager said in August that per-lot mowing 'we don't have that tracked in a system' (First Alert 4, 14 Aug 2026). Both can be true: a billing charge is not an operations log.
2025 holds 13,168 cut rows on 8,780 parcels against 46,346 on 16,118 in 2026; why is not established.

chain.title: Single light out, 'work completed', by ward group (failed robustness)

chain.title: Cave-ins: referral versus repair
chain.plain: In the southwest, cave-in requests are mostly closed within a day as 'referred to street maintenance for repair work to be scheduled'; in the north the same referral takes about six weeks. Where the words say 'work completed' the wait is about 8 days against 23, but too few southwest repairs are recorded that way to call it proven.

chain.title: Silently cancelled tree requests in Forestry's work orders
chain.plain: We checked the addresses of silently cancelled tree requests against the city's public lists of tree work orders. They turn up there about five times as often as unrelated requests; and where they match an open removal order, the order was usually already open long before the resident called (a median of about 19 months), so the request was folded into an old backlog without a word.
chain.label: observed

sources.name: 311 service requests (Citizens' Service Bureau), yearly CSVs in csb.zip

joins: Normalised 311 address matched to the work order's WoAddress (same normaliser); N1 also tests within 30 m (19.2%, no spatial baseline).
corrections: Softened from 'most cancelled tree requests were converted to work orders': requests closed 'work order created' match at only 6.8%, so the address match misses most true pairs (COMMON's 2.4% was all closed tree requests).
Re-read by N5: the usual pattern is 'already on the backlog, and nobody said so', not conversion.
bounds: Samples hold about a third of the work orders (1,500 of 2,522 removals; 1,500 of 6,276 trims), so absolute rates are lower bounds.
Only the city's public saved searches were used.

Parcel to the LRA inventory (city-owned) and to the ledger.
corrections: Counted once per REQUESTID: the city's CSV repeats a request once per caller (349,031 rows hold 322,104 requests in 2024-26).

The ledger is a billing record, not an operations log: SERVICEDATE is a posting date batched by about a week (8,507 of 2026's rows carry a Sunday date; 2,608 carry 23 April), so day counts are precise to the week, and a cut that was never billed looks like no cut. Say 'no cut billed', never 'never cut'.
bounds: Shown at block level only, including the hero lot (Jack's ruling); ids withheld from public files.

Use N5's 94 requests on 75 lots (N8 settled; independent recompute 90 on 71, the gap is the address join). N6's brief count of 103 on 82 drops the resident filter and uses N1's wider join; it must say 'all channels' or adopt N5's rule. Requests filed after mid-September have had little time: filed by 15 Sep, 79 on 62 (N8).

Lot-1 drew a 'vacant lot cut incomplete' call on 9 Sep 2026, closed 'supervisor notified', and the receipt shows it; the narration must address it, not scroll past it (N8 finding 1). Such calls do not prove a cut: of 2026 'cut incomplete' calls matched to a parcel, N5 counts 63 of 227 filed within 30 days after a billed cut and 40 on lots with no cut billed all year; N8's independent count is 67 of 229 and 61 (rule difference not yet reconciled).
Lot 3's story names a possible innocent explanation (an accepted land-bank offer).

chain.title: Land-bank lots closed 'on schedule' with no cut billed after
chain.plain: Among city-owned vacant lots that residents reported for weeds in 2026 and that the city closed within three days as 'on schedule to be cut', 94 requests on 75 lots show no cut billed in the city's own ledger afterwards. The lead example, on the 1700 block of N Taylor Av, was reported twice and closed within minutes both times; 36 other parcels on its city block were billed for cuts that season, and it was not.

n6_brief_pothole_first_week_below_half.period: residential pothole requests filed 6 Apr to 4 Oct 2026, closed by 13 Oct 2026
n6_brief_pothole_first_week_below_half.definition: First week of 2026 in which fewer than half of closed residential pothole requests (at least 15) were closed within CityStat's 8-day goal.
n6_brief_pothole_first_week_below_half.label: observed
n6_brief_pothole_first_week_below_half.derivation: 311 requests (City of St. Louis open data, csb.zip yearly CSVs, invalid bytes dropped, one row per request number), as loaded by N1 into build/stl.duckdb; residential pothole requests grouped by the week filed; share of closed requests closed within 8 days of filing (CityStat's goal and definition C, which N4 found reproduces CityStat's counts); weeks with fewer than 15 closed requests not used. e3_queue_open_since_2025.period: open requests filed 2025-01-01 to 2026-10-13, as of 2026-10-13 23:59 Central (public file data through 2026-10-13 00:33)
e3_queue_open_since_2025.definition: Open requests (status not closed or cancelled) filed on or after 1 January 2025.
e3_queue_open_since_2025.label: observed
e3_queue_open_since_2025.source_sql_or_script: scripts/exec/E3/build_queue.py :: SELECT count(DISTINCT request_id) FROM requests WHERE ts_init >= '2025-01-01' AND status_group = 'open'
e3_queue_open_since_2025.derivation: Counted by REQUESTID in the public 311 file: every request filed since 1 Jan 2025 whose status is still open on the run date (16,505).

e3_queue_past_promise.period: open requests filed 2025-01-01 to 2026-10-13, as of 2026-10-13 23:59 Central (public file data through 2026-10-13 00:33)
e3_queue_past_promise.definition: Open requests filed since 1 January 2025 whose promised date (the city's own PRJCOMPLETEDATE, shown on its status page as 'Dept Response Due By') is before the run date.
e3_queue_past_promise.label: observed
e3_queue_past_promise.source_sql_or_script: scripts/exec/E3/build_queue.py :: SELECT count(DISTINCT request_id) FROM requests WHERE ts_init >= '2025-01-01' AND status_group = 'open' AND ts_promised < '2026-10-13 23:59:59'
e3_queue_past_promise.note: Includes 329 requests of sensitive types (encampments, welfare checks, discrimination, legal claims, police referrals), counted in totals and division rows only; never on the map, list or CSV.
e3_queue_past_promise.derivation: Counted by REQUESTID in the public 311 file: of 16,505 open requests filed since 1 Jan 2025, 14,902 carry a promised date before 13 Oct 2026 23:59 Central. 89 open requests have no promised date and are left out. Matches the orchestrator's one-pass count (14,902).

e3_queue_past_promise_share.period: open requests filed 2025-01-01 to 2026-10-13, as of 2026-10-13 23:59 Central (public file data through 2026-10-13 00:33)
e3_queue_past_promise_share.definition: Share of open requests filed since 1 January 2025 that are past their promised date.
e3_queue_past_promise_share.label: observed
e3_queue_past_promise_share.derivation: 14,902 past promise / 16,505 open, both counted by REQUESTID in the public 311 file.

e3_queue_past_180.period: open requests filed 2025-01-01 to 2026-10-13, as of 2026-10-13 23:59 Central (public file data through 2026-10-13 00:33)
e3_queue_past_180.definition: Open requests filed since 1 January 2025 that are more than 180 days past their promised date.
e3_queue_past_180.label: observed
e3_queue_past_180.source_sql_or_script: scripts/exec/E3/build_queue.py :: ... AND date_diff('day', CAST(ts_promised AS DATE), DATE '2026-10-13') > 180
e3_queue_past_180.derivation: Days past promise = calendar days from the promised date to 13 Oct 2026 (the same rule as N1's monday_list view). 6,724 of the 14,902 are more than 180 days past. Matches the orchestrator's one-pass count (6,724).
